Dont Panic Then It'S Not Smoke @Fizzhogg23But What If There’S A Burning Smell With The White Smoke ? ​@Adriananzures3213 The "Smoke" Is Condenswater I Want To Know How That Trans Fluid Got Into The Engine Same Here Yeah, And The First One Would Be Steam Not Smoke. @Rob-Fc9Wg  Your Wrong Sorry. Nothing Is Steam. Rear Main Seal Blow Out. @Saiko8096 
Please Explain How Water Entering The Combustion Chamber Turns To Smoke. So Basically What You’Re Telling Me Is My Car Shouldn’T Be Giving Out Any Smoke Which Means Literally Any Car I’Ve Ever Had Or Seen Is Broken Or Has Some Sort Of Problem If There'S Any Type Of Visible Smoke Being Emitted By The Exhaust?  Yes. The First One Could Be Also Humidity In The Air, Especially If You Live In A Cooler Climate Wrong.  Humidity (Aka: Water) Boils And Becomes Water Vapor (Not Steam As Some Believe, Since Steam Is Invisible).  Coolant, However, Being 50-70% Ethyl-Glycol, Turns Into A Hot Chemical Cloud, Thick Enough To Appear As Smoke, On The Level Of A James Bondian Smoke Screen.  They Are Not The Same. White Smoke On A Really Cold Day Is No Big Deal.  In Diesel Cars White Smoke Can Also Be The Diesel Particulate Filter Dpf Clearing Out Or Clogged If The Dpf Is "Clogged" Your Engine Wouldn'T Be Running. White: It Got No Gas
Blue: Exhaust Coloring
Grey: Normal Car Color
Black: Rolling Coal  I Get White Smoke From My Mgb When The Carb Is Set To Rich At Tick Over. Adjust The Mixture Using A Wideband And It Goes Away, So It'S Not Always Coolant.  Amend The White Smoke To Say Humidity Caused By Temperature Differences.... It'S Not Always Coolant  What I Can Confirm Is. When My Truck Gets Black Smoke, Then It'S Time To Change Air Intake Filter...😂  If Your Air Filter Is Blocked This Can Cause The Black Smoke Too  Which Color Is Normal And Indicates That The Car Is In Good Condition? Generally It Should Be Pretty Clear On A Warm Day. On A Cold Day It'Ll Look White And Foggy (Like When You Can See Your Breath) None.  Any Visible Smoke Means There'S Something Wrong With Your Car'S Engine. ​@Rotorhead1651 Really Depends Which Car You Have. 

I Have A 20 Years Old Honda, Off Course Is Burning Coolant And Oil Which End Up In The Engine, Because The Car Is Very Old And The Seals Are Not Tight Anymore, But This Car Can Also Make Another 300K Miles This Way :). 

It Has A Big Engine And Still Going Strong. 
( 2.2 ). 

With A 1.4 Engine, If You Have Any Fluid In Your Engine That Is Not Diesel Or Petrol, Your Engine Will Die. But That'S Another Story If You Drive A Rotary "No Smoke" Means Your Car Is Dead 😂
